messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Markdown to WordPress
parts:
I'm not sure how Tyler made it, so I'm just Cc'ing him. My guess is
the post was manually edited: [sourcecode][/sourcecode] in the post
source was replace by <pre></pre>.

It is possible to automate this, but I do not have much time for it at
the moment, so please file an issue
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues if you really need such a
feature. As I mentioned at http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/wordpress/, I
think syntax highlighting via highlight.js is better (totally my own
opinion), but I'm not sure if wordpress.com allows that.

Regards,
Yihui
--

On Mon, Nov 11, 2013 at 9:14 PM, dogle <do...@northland.edu> wrote:
> All,
>
> I have been trying to use knitr with markdown and knit2wp() to write "blog"
> entries with wordpress.com. For the most part I have been successful.
> However, the output from a chunk appears with the same format (row numbers
> and syntax highlighting) as the input R code for the chunk. For example,
> see http://fishr.wordpress.com/2013/11/11/merge-relational-dataframes/. I
> have tried unsuccessfully to find a solution to this and have noticed that
> both this
> (http://wkmor1.wordpress.com/2012/07/01/rchievement-of-the-day-3-bloggin-from-r-14/)
> and this
> (http://yihui.wordpress.com/2013/02/10/a-test-of-knitr-and-wordpress/) have
> the same "problem", but this
> (http://trinkerrstuff.wordpress.com/2013/03/19/knitr2wordpress-and-gradient_cloud-revisited-16/)
> does not.
>
> Here is the only part of my markdown file that is not simply R calculations
> ...
>
> ```{r setup, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
> # Having this separate from the setup file allows one to knit this in
> RStudio.
> opts_chunk$set(dev="png",tidy=FALSE)
> ```
>
> I run this code to make the page that is sent to Wordpress.com
>
> ## Run these commands when you are ready to push out to the fishR blog.
> title <- "Merge Relational Dataframes"
> cats <- c('Data Manipulation')
> keys <- c('Data Manipulation')
> setwd("C:/aaaWork/Web/fishR/BlogExamples")
> source('WPSetup.R')
> knit2wp("MergeRelationalDataframes.Rmd",publish=FALSE,shortcode=TRUE,
> title=title,categories=cats,mt_keywords=keys)
>
> where the WPSetup.R file looks like this (with username, password, and
> dropbox location changed for this e-mail) ...
>
> # Load RWordPress and knitr
> library(RWordPress)
> library(knitr)
>
> # Set some knitr options
> opts_knit$set(base.url = "http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/figure/",
> base.dir = "C:/Users/dogle/Dropbox/figure/")
>
> # Set some R options to use WordPress
> options(WordpressLogin=c(user="password"),
> WordpressURL="http://fishr.wordpress.com/xmlrpc.php")
>
> I am using R 3.0.2, RStudio -0.98.456, and knitr 1.5 on a Windows 7 machine.
>
> If anybody has any suggestions I would be greatly appreciative. Thank you
> in advance for any help you can offer.

messages.author: 2f7f86025d764105
messages.subject: RE: [knitr] Markdown to WordPress [Content Policy Infringement]
parts:
Tyler and Yihui,

 

Thanks for your time with this.  I will just use a manual edit for now.

 

I did look, briefly, into knit2wp() in the hopes that I could easily modify that.  A problem is that both the input and output sections originally end with the same </code></pre> (making it hard to provide an automated way to end with [\sourcecode] for the input and </pre> for the output).  I also thought that I could use these hooks (and shortcode=FALSE) but that also did not seem to work for me …

 

knit_hooks$set(

  input = function(x,options) paste('[sourcecode language="r"',x,'[/sourcecode]',sep='')

  output = function(x,options) paste('<pre>\n',x,'</pre>\n',sep='')

)

 

I will submit the issue as suggested and do a manual edit for now … this functionality of knitr is still leaps-and-bound above where I was without it.  Again, thank you very much for your time.

From: Tyler Rinker [mailto:tyler....@gmail.com]
Sent: Wednesday, November 13, 2013 10:25 AM
To: kn...@googlegroups.com
Cc: Derek Ogle; Tyler Rinker
Subject: Re: [knitr] Markdown to WordPress [Content Policy Infringement]

 

Yihui's suspicions are correct.  I manually edited.  I, like, Yihui could rework this but when I weigh the time cost of coding it with the frequency that I would use it, a manual edit is a more efficient use of my time.

 

If you have the time and know how I'd also suggest you do a pull request if you're able.


Tyler
